target_customer: Crop breeders and seed companies working on vegetables, fruits and nuts
problem: Gene editing needs stem cell transformation that works only for a few crops; many crops resist editing.
business_model: Editing platform and trait development for breeders (model not public)

founders.name: Matej Zamecnik
education: MS Plant Experimental Biology, Masaryk University
previous_startups: Spicy Cells, bioreactors for saffron cell cultures, outcome not stated

competitors.name: Pairwise
competitors.what: Licenses Fulcrum CRISPR platform, develops fruit traits
competitors.traction_then: 25 licensees across 30+ species per later report

competitors.name: Inari
competitors.what: Multiplex CRISPR for soy, corn and wheat

competitors.name: Cibus
competitors.what: Gene edited traits, now focused on rapeseed
competitors.traction_then: Gene edited oil never reached scale per source
competitors.funding_then: Q2 2026 net loss $22.1M, cash into early 2027

technical_complexity.rationale: Editing via CRISPR delivered into pollen across many crop species is research grade; the team won the iGEM Grand Prize for duckweed work.

defensibility.rationale: A novel delivery route could be patentable, but unproven across crops; established licensers exist.

market_need_then: Trade press says editing is getting faster but commercialization is not; breeders need tools for crops that resist transformation.

branding.name_origin: Starts as the NitroDuck iGEM project, a duckweed system converting cattle urine into protein biomass, per university and press coverage

identity.voice_and_tone: Playful tagline 'Monsanto for yummy crops, but without pesticides'

brand_strength.rationale: Memorable playful name tied to an iGEM project that won Grand Prize in 2025 per university news; the duck reference may mismatch pollen editing.

pivots.from: NitroDuck duckweed vertical farm for protein from urine (iGEM project)
pivots.to: CRISPR editing of crops via pollen
pivots.why: Not stated by a source; inferred from change in described product, so treat as unconfirmed

outcome_analysis: Nitroduck grew from the iGEM Brno NitroDuck duckweed project and now pitches CRISPR delivery through pollen for hard to edit crops. The team has strong academic credentials but crop biotech is slow and capital heavy, with well funded rivals. No funding or exit was found, so there is no outcome yet.
notes: Funding search found only an unrelated company named Nitrode. Pivot entry is an inference from sources describing an earlier project; no source calls it a pivot. Gries and Rosputinsky education not on YC page. Competitor entries are 2026 and are as of the batch.
